public_rationale: SATBench's September 22, 2025 version varies clause counts and reports answer errors on logical puzzles, meeting the condition of larger and harder propositional inputs [e1]. These results do not isolate internal encoding failure [e1]. The December 6, 2024 probing study reports that its similarity measure misses distinctions in a three-entity example that interventions still detect; the authors suggest their methods may be too noisy for contexts with more than two entities [e2]. Neither item establishes systematic encoding failure or robust encoding across substantial increases in logical complexity [e1, e2].
limitations: Answer accuracy does not distinguish encoding errors from reasoning or decoding errors [e1].
The probing study does not establish encoding reliability at the larger logical complexity contemplated by the claim [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As propositions become more numerous and complex, LLMs' encoding of them will also prove unreliable.
conditions: as number and complexity of propositions increases

statement.excerpt: As the number of propositions and the complexity of what is represented increases (e.g., to include logical quantifiers), I expect encoding too will turn out to be unreliable.
statement.document_title: Generative AI’s crippling and widespread failure to induce robust models of the world

from_speaker: As the number of propositions and the complexity of what is represented increases
I expect encoding too will turn out to be unreliable
our_interpretation: Encoding means the internal representation of the supplied propositions, distinguished from producing an answer or decoding that representation.
The antecedent is exposure to larger and more complex propositional inputs. Quantifiers are an example, not a required feature of every test.
Increasing the number of interacting Boolean clauses is an ordinary instance of increasing proposition count and represented logical complexity.
The forecast concerns systematic encoding failures, not an isolated mistake or a requirement that every model fail on every larger input.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled experiments with larger and more complex propositional inputs demonstrate systematic loss or corruption of their internal representation, with controls separating encoding failure from probe, reasoning, and decoding failure.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Well-controlled experiments across substantial increases in proposition count and logical complexity establish robust internal encoding, including on cases where generated answers fail.

evidence.explanation: SATBench tests models on logical puzzles with varying clause counts and difficulty, satisfying the antecedent under the stated reading. Its answer-level errors do not identify whether internal encoding, reasoning, or decoding failed.

evidence.excerpt: our current methods may be too noisy
evidence.locator: Section 5.3, qualitative evaluation of binding similarity
evidence.explanation: The authors distinguish shortcomings in their probe from shortcomings in the model's representation: interventions still capture binding differences that the similarity measure misses. Consequently, poorer probing performance on larger inputs cannot alone settle Marcus's prediction.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Reproducible experiments that increase proposition count and logical complexity, measure internal representations with validated methods, and establish systematic encoding failure or robust encoding while separating probe, reasoning, and decoding errors.
